text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, you’ve got a clean one ahead, with clear skies holding through 6:46 and a comfortable 68 degrees now. After dark, the temperature slips quickly, landing near 46 by morning with only a light north breeze. The air is crisp and clean, so this is a good evening for a walk, but bring a layer for the trip home.

Friday looks mostly sunny and a little warmer, with a high around 70, though the models range from the upper 60s to the mid 70s. I’d bet on the low 70s, with a north wind of 5 to 12 mph. The lake stays fairly manageable, with waves around 1 to 2 feet, but it’ll still feel cool near the water. Plan on a jacket after sunset tonight, and a comfortable waterfront day Friday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): The coastal low meandering off southern New England will bring cool, showery, and breezy weather on Sunday. Waves of rain showers will sweep across the region (60% chance), with the heaviest rainfall focused across southern and eastern Vermont where totals of half an inch to an inch are possible. Northerly winds will be breezy, gusting 20 to 25 mph in valley locations and stronger across Lake Champlain and mountain summits, keeping Sunday’s highs cool in the lower 60s. Showers taper off Monday (30% chance) as the storm shifts eastward, leaving partly sunny skies and highs near 63°. High pressure then builds back in for Tuesday and Wednesday, bringing full sunshine and pleasant temperatures warming from 61° Tuesday to 68° Wednesday.
